attrs.evidence: Every candidate imported from INV-R7.5 carries imported_from.source_status as provenance and readjudicated{by, on, method, authority_transferred:false} as the target lane's own act; the gate reads the second and refuses any record where the flag is not false, and since INV-R9.2 it also binds the first to the pinned material — the ledger's imported_from must name the revision AND the artifact the manifest pins, and the source status it records must be the status that artifact actually carries. The methods are witness_reran_on_target for PROVED (the named gate executes in this candidate's gate run), question_survives for OPEN, redeclared_by_target for DECLARED, citation_recheck for KNOWN, carried_provisional for PROVISIONAL, and historical_refutation_preserved for REFUTED, whose refutation_scope names a source-lane revision and stays a fact about that revision. THE STATUS HISTOGRAM IS NOT STATED HERE: check-integration §histogram derives it per disposition from the bucket records. INV-R9 typed one into this field and it summed to 35 while describing 34 imports, because the fifteenth PROVED candidate is the one disposed as already_present — INC-R9-HISTOGRAM-DRIFT.
attrs.gap: RE-ADJUDICATION BY METHOD IS NOT RE-ADJUDICATION BY JUDGEMENT. The gate checks that a method is recorded and that the witness resolves and runs; it cannot check that the method FITS the claim — a PROVED claim whose gate exits zero for a reason unrelated to its obligation passes here exactly as it would have on the source lane. Second: `redeclared_by_target` is the weakest of the six and covers six records; a declaration re-declared in bulk is a declaration nobody re-read. Third: the 8 forwarded shared-claim corrections took the same treatment, which is defensible because 0 of them collided, and would not be if any had.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/check-integration.mjs — the authority_transferred and status-agreement checks
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6 adjudication §4: statuses never transfer AUTOMATICALLY; re-establishment may rerun a witness, reuse an unchanged content-addressed proof whose applicability assumptions still hold, re-check a cited theorem mapping, or reject the claim.
attrs.review_focus: Six DECLARED records were re-declared in one operation. Is bulk re-declaration honest, or should a declaration require an act per record — and what would distinguish the two mechanically?
attrs.statement: A source-lane claim status is not authoritative on the target lane until target-lane adjudication re-establishes its applicability; every imported record carries its source status as provenance and a separate record of the target's own act.
